#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=federaser
#   --nodes=1
#   --mem=50000
#   -o tensor_out_3.txt
#   -e tensor_error_3.txt
#   --partition=gpu
#   --gres=gpu:1

#flux: --job-name=federaser
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --output=tensor_out_3.txt
#flux: --error=tensor_error_3.txt

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=50000
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: --partition=gpu and --gres=gpu:1
# Flux queue/partition and GPU requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled without a GPU (or on non-GPU nodes), causing failure or severe slowdown.

module load cuda/10.0.130
module load anaconda/3.6

source activate federaser

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, run within the allocation (optionally via flux run -n 1).
python ../Fed_Unlearn_main_3.py

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`, `--partition=gpu`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.
The original Slurm job requested memory (`--mem=50000`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.
